description: §17.6.2 — a nested VALUE-FORM DECLARATION inside an if-as-expression arm body is a side effect of the arm, not a designation of its result. `#out-nested-if` puts a `const inner = if (…) { lift … }` ahead of the arm's own `lift`; `#out-nested-if-else` pins that the ELSE limb of the outer if still resolves correctly when the then-arm carrying the nested declaration is not taken; `#out-nested-for` does the same with a for-as-expression comprehension; `#out-two-nested` chains TWO nested declarations before the designating `lift` and combines both. Only the outer `lift` designates the outer result.
rationale: The S395 ruling's operative sentence is categorical: only a `lift` — or the §17.6.10 single-expression sugar — designates an arm's result value. A nested value-form declaration binds its result to an IDENTIFIER (`inner` / `picked` / `first` / `second`), so it is not a designating form and §32.2 does not reach it either (that rule is scoped to "an expression statement whose value is not bound to any identifier"). Before the fix, the parent-context propagation tail shared by emitIfExprDecl / emitForExprDecl / emitMatchExprDecl repointed the ENCLOSING arm's tilde context at the nested construct's own result variable, so the outer `lift` wrote the INNER variable and the outer binding stayed at its §17.6.4 `null` seed — silent-wrong at exit 0 with zero diagnostics, exactly the ctrl-025 signature one nesting level down. The outer `else` limb then assigned a name block-scoped to the outer THEN branch, which in the emitted classic script is a silent implicit global; `#out-nested-if-else` is the selector that pins that limb. §17.6.8 grants the compiler latitude over the emitted JavaScript, so this case asserts OBSERVABLE RESULTS, not emitted-code shape.
